transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

People keep telling me I’m not listening. My supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught part of what they said and have to ask them to repeat it.
Did you experience similar trouble paying attention when you were a child in school?

Yeah, definitely. Even before middle school, teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t stay put. I’d call out answers instead of waiting, and I got in trouble for butting into other kids’ work.
Nowadays, do you find yourself feeling restless or having trouble sitting still?
Yeah. When I have to sit still, it feels like pressure building up in my chest and legs. Like I’ve got to move or do something right then, or I’ll crawl out of my skin.

latest_inference.note: Presence of both significant inattentive and hyperactive/restless symptoms persisting from childhood into adulthood confirms a combined presentation, ruling out predominantly inattentive type (F90.0).
